title: Sideband fingerprint of the Leggett mode in terahertz two-dimensional coherent spectroscopy of multiband superconductors
authors: Silvia Neri, Ryo Shimano, Dirk Manske, Naoto Tsuji
abstract: Collective modes of the superconducting condensate encode fundamental information on the pairing interaction, yet their direct detection remains experimentally challenging. In multiband superconductors, the Leggett mode, i.e., a coherent oscillation of the relative phase between two condensates, is Raman-active and couples to light only nonlinearly in ordinary situations. Here we show theoretically that terahertz two-dimensional coherent spectroscopy (2DCS) provides a direct fingerprint of the Leggett mode (with frequency $ω_L$) through sideband emission at the detection frequency $ω_t = ω_L\pmΩ$ ($Ω$ is the central frequency of the incident pulses) in the nonlinear 2D spectrum. The key insight is that the finite duration of the THz pulses is the physical mechanism that makes the mode accessible: the broad spectral content of a finite pulse provides the nonlinear frequency combinations needed to resonantly excite the mode at ωL without any prior knowledge of its value or tuning of external parameters. We demonstrate robustness of this signature against temperature and quasiparticle relaxation, and show that sweeping $Ω$ allows unambiguous identification of the Leggett mode.
summary: This work theoretically establishes that terahertz two-dimensional coherent spectroscopy (2DCS) can directly fingerprint the elusive Leggett mode in multiband superconductors. The key insight is that the finite duration of the THz pulses enables the nonlinear excitation of this mode, which appears as distinct sidebands in the 2D spectrum. This method offers a powerful, non-invasive diagnostic tool for studying superconducting pairing interactions.
main_problem: The primary challenge is the direct experimental detection of collective superconducting modes, specifically the Leggett mode, which are difficult to observe in multiband superconductors.
main_result: The authors theoretically demonstrate that terahertz two-dimensional coherent spectroscopy (2DCS) provides a unique and robust fingerprint of the Leggett mode through characteristic sideband emission in the nonlinear 2D spectrum.
method: The theoretical framework involves calculating the nonlinear dynamics of the superconducting order parameters using the Anderson pseudospin language and analyzing the resulting third-order nonlinear current to predict the 2D spectrum.
model_or_system: The system is a multiband superconductor, modeled using a minimal two-band BCS framework, whose dynamics are mapped onto pseudospin equations. The Leggett mode represents the coherent oscillation of the relative phase between the two superconducting condensates.
key_observables: The Leggett mode frequency ($\omega_L$), which manifests as sidebands in the 2D spectrum at $\omega_t = \omega_L \pm \Omega$.

main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Random Phase Approximation (RPA) and assumes the finite duration of the THz pulses provides the necessary nonlinear frequency mixing to excite the mode.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the comparison between conventional 2D spectroscopy and the predicted 2DCS spectrum, showing the characteristic side peaks associated with the Leggett mode.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the physical difficulty of measuring the mode to deriving the theoretical signature using 2DCS, demonstrating its robustness against dissipation, and finally showing unambiguous identification by sweeping the central frequency $\Omega$.
why_interesting: The use of nonlinear spectroscopy (2DCS) to probe a collective, non-linear excitation like the Leggett mode is highly relevant to open quantum systems and quantum optics, as it requires understanding how coherent driving fields couple to intrinsic many-body dynamics.
